batches.meaning: Final consumer/lifecycle and critical button/window regressions with test CLI telemetry disabled; installation delay still variable.

beforeAfter.conclusion: The 20-run batch took longer than the recorded baseline. CLI installation time is highly variable. This is evidence for repeatable orchestration and input/result accounting, not a controlled speed benchmark or a 2x gain. No assertion cases or native host/window cleanup boundaries were removed.

limitations: Windows remains deferred and requires native references of its own OS.
Case IDs enumerate published driver results, not every internal assertion.
Existing legacy assertion failures may remain unclassified.
Test CLI telemetry is disabled, but installation timing variability is unresolved.
No GUI hosts are shared; CLI installs are intentionally repeated per isolated profile.
A Code wrapper hash identifies the wrapper; it does not attest its underlying executable.
Application workspace inputs are external and not frozen by the optional application suite.
Rust source and backend are recorded separately; no assertion of a fresh Rust build/check is made by this test-only change.
